reasoning: Graphs on 15 vertices with girth >=8 have maximum degree mostly <=2 (trees or unicyclic with cycles >=8), yielding at most 15 edges. Higher degrees require branching vertices separated by distance ~4 with paths ensuring all cycles >=8. Constructions (e.g., multiple paths between 2-3 high-degree vertices) achieve at most ~17-18 edges before short cycles (C3-C7) appear due to pigeonhole on path lengths/multiplicities or insufficient vertices (Moore-like: deg>=3 vertex with branching needs ~10-22 exclusive verts). For 24 edges, sum(deg-2)=18 implies ~9+ high-degree vertices or high multiplicities, forcing support graph on them to have 18+ edges, which (even if triangle-free) creates weighted cycles summing to <8. Bipartite case limits to <=22 edges even without C4 alone (sum binom(d_y,2) <= binom(7,2)=21). Thus, impossible to reach 24 edges.
